summary: Fresh FOC Heat research. The next verified FOC window is Monday, Aug. 31, 2026. That Texas Blood: Hell Comes to Allison Ranch #1 is the strongest current risk-adjusted BUY at one standard copy near cover price. Midnight X-Men #1, Wolverine: Paradise #1, Crimes Against Nature #1, Midnight Spider-Man #1, and Midnight Fantastic Four #1 remain WATCH rather than BUY because comic-specific aftermarket demand is not yet demonstrated. Doom All-On-One #1 and Vampirella X Witchblade Special #1 are PASS.
orderingWindow: Now through Monday, Aug. 31, 2026. PRH identifies Aug. 31 as the FOC date; M&M Comics states weekly FOC orders are due 7pm Central every Monday, and specifically lists Aug. 31 items at 8pm CDT. For an Indianapolis/Eastern-time retailer using that clock, 8pm EDT is the corresponding time, but retailer-specific deadlines can differ.

books.title: THAT TEXAS BLOOD: HELL COMES TO ALLISON RANCH #1 (OF 6)
verifiedFacts: Image describes this as a six-issue miniseries premiere and a new number one in the That Texas Blood series.
Image lists 40 pages and a $4.99 cover price.
The story returns to Ambrose County and follows Sheriff Joe Bob Coates and Deputy Wilson Hart at the Allison Ranch in 2003.
Comic Previews and multiple current retailers list Aug. 31, 2026 as FOC; Rune Works specifically identifies the 1:25 Mark Chiarello incentive with the same cutoff.
marketEvidence: Completed-sale evidence for the original That Texas Blood #1 remains materially above cover for many standard copies. PriceCharting currently reports roughly $20 ungraded and shows recent completed sales including $29.99, $28.40, $24.85, $19.99 and $14.99.
Other standard/variant copies of the original #1 sell materially lower, including several recent sales around $5-$15, so the franchise has demand but not uniform scarcity.
The series has additional real-world demand signaling from announced FX development, but that is not treated as proof of aftermarket appreciation.
books.thesis: This is the clearest current BUY because the underlying franchise has demonstrated aftermarket demand on its original #1 while the new issue still has a low cover-price entry. The key risk is supply: the original issue's market is mixed, and a new number one can be ordered heavily. One standard copy is justified; buying multiple copies or expensive incentives is not.
unknowns: Whether the new story creates a new key or first appearance
Whether TV development materially increases demand for this specific issue
Post-release completed sales for the new #1

books.title: MIDNIGHT: X-MEN #1
books.creators: Jonathan Hickman (writer), Matteo Della Fonte (artist), Dike Ruan (Cover A)
verifiedFacts: Marvel lists Oct. 7, 2026 on-sale and Aug. 31, 2026 FOC.
The series is a new Midnight Universe launch built around vampires, mutant factions and an impending war.
The debut has a broad variant program including recurring Midnight themes and multiple virgin/ratio-style variants.
marketEvidence: There are no completed sales for the unreleased issue, so comic-specific demand cannot yet be demonstrated.

Hickman's 2019 X-Men #1 has active completed-sale history, but many standard and common variants remain near cover; that is evidence of collector interest, not proof that Midnight X-Men will appreciate.
Marvel's extensive variant architecture increases collector attention but also raises supply risk.
books.thesis: The creative team and launch positioning make this the strongest of the three Midnight books on paper, but the evidence does not support a BUY. Hickman's name is not enough to repeat the project's Minotaur error. WATCH for retailer sell-through, first-appearance/key information, and post-release completed sales.
unknowns: Whether the Midnight Universe develops durable collector demand

books.title: WOLVERINE: PARADISE #1
verifiedFacts: PRH lists Oct. 14, 2026 on-sale, Aug. 31, 2026 FOC, $4.99 and 40 pages.
The premise puts Logan in Miami against a criminal underworld and guest-stars Dazzler.
The book is presented as an auteur-driven Wolverine story by Dan Panosian.
marketEvidence: Recent completed sales for Dan Panosian's Absolute Flash #1 card-stock variant are generally around $1-$6, showing that creator credit alone does not create a premium.
His Pop Kill #1 variant has recent completed sales around $5-$7, again close to entry price.
There is no completed-sale evidence for Wolverine: Paradise #1 because it is unreleased.
books.thesis: Interesting because Wolverine is a major collector character and Panosian is handling both writing and art, but the market evidence does not establish a scarcity or demand imbalance. WATCH, with a standard copy only if later evidence supports it at cover or below.
unknowns: Whether the new status quo contains a major key event

books.title: CRIMES AGAINST NATURE #1
verifiedFacts: Image lists a Sept. 23, 2026 release and $3.99 cover price.
It is a new series about a Hollywood animal trainer and his gorilla client/friend being framed for a crime.
Current catalog data lists 1:25 Tyler Boss and 1:50 Mattia Monaco incentives plus a Witchblade team-up cover.
Comic Previews and current retailers list Aug. 31 as FOC.
marketEvidence: No completed-sale evidence exists for the unreleased comic.
Current guide estimates for the unreleased variants are not treated as completed-sale evidence.
The low $3.99 entry reduces downside, but there is no verified demand signal strong enough to justify a BUY.
books.thesis: The premise is differentiated and the price is attractive, but this is still an unproven new IP. The 1:25/1:50 structure is not enough by itself. WATCH for early retailer demand and actual sales.
unknowns: Whether the unusual premise converts to collector demand

books.title: MIDNIGHT: SPIDER-MAN #1
books.creators: Phillip Kennedy Johnson (writer), ScieTronc (artist), Steve Beach (Cover A)
verifiedFacts: Current Marvel catalog data lists Oct. 7, 2026 on-sale and Aug. 31, 2026 FOC.
The launch has a large multi-cover program including Peach Momoko, Jeehyung Lee, InHyuk Lee and a Clayton Crain connecting variant.
Collect Forever currently offers the standard issue and lists a later pre-order deadline for its own e-pack product, which is separate from distributor FOC.
marketEvidence: There are no completed sales for the unreleased issue.
The breadth of variants is evidence of collector-targeted publishing, but also of potentially high supply.
No verified issue-specific scarcity or key event currently supports paying above cover.
books.thesis: Spider-Man provides a much larger collector base than most new launches, but that is exactly why supply risk is high. WATCH; do not chase variants before actual demand is established.
unknowns: Which variants, if any, will retain premiums

books.title: MIDNIGHT: FANTASTIC FOUR #1
books.creators: Benjamin Percy (writer), Kev Walker (artist), Kev Walker (Cover A)
verifiedFacts: Marvel catalog data lists Oct. 7, 2026 on-sale and Aug. 31, 2026 FOC.
The issue is part of the new Midnight Universe and uses the same broad variant program as the other Midnight launches.
The debut has recurring Midnight Bloodbath, horror-homage, gallery and connecting-cover themes.
marketEvidence: No completed sales exist for the unreleased issue.
The Fantastic Four name supplies a substantial collector audience, but likely also supports substantial ordering.
No verified issue-specific scarcity or major first appearance has been established.
books.thesis: A legitimate collector-interest book but not a demonstrated investment opportunity yet. WATCH at cover price; do not buy ratios based solely on the franchise name.

books.title: DOOM ALL-ON-ONE #1
verifiedFacts: PRH lists Oct. 14, 2026 on-sale, Aug. 31 FOC, 64 pages and a $7.99 cover price.
The story is a large-format Doom-versus-the-Marvel-Universe spectacle.
The issue has additional covers/incentives.
marketEvidence: No completed-sale evidence exists for the unreleased issue.
The $7.99 entry price raises the break-even hurdle for an investment purchase.
Creator and character strength do not establish demand exceeding supply.
books.thesis: Potentially desirable as a reading/collector book, but the investment case is weak at $7.99 without evidence of scarcity or a durable key. PASS.

books.title: VAMPIRELLA X WITCHBLADE SPECIAL #1
books.creators: Erica Schultz (writer), Valentina Pinti (artist); covers by Stjepan Sejic, Lucio Parrillo, Francesco Mattina, Carla Cohen, Joseph Michael Linsner and others
verifiedFacts: Dynamite and current Comic Previews data list Sept. 23 release and Aug. 31 FOC.
The issue is a 48-page Vampirella/Witchblade crossover with a premium mystery blind-bag program.
The standard cover price is $5.99 and a 1:15 Linsner incentive is being solicited.
marketEvidence: Recent completed sales for the 2026 Vampirella #1 show the standard Cover A around $3.33-$4.99 and multiple common/ratio variants around or below cover, demonstrating that variant scarcity alone has not consistently produced durable premiums.
Some Vampirella blind-bag and limited variants have sold higher, but those results are not sufficient to establish demand for this new crossover.
No completed sales exist for the unreleased crossover.
books.thesis: Recognizable characters and a broad variant program create collector interest, but the recent Vampirella market is not strong enough to justify buying this at $5.99 for investment. PASS.
